3. It is further plaint case that Kutiron and Rubzan were the owners of 5 annas 6 gonda 2 Kara 2 Kranti share of Khatian No. 30 together with 4 annas share of Khatian No. 1104. Plaintiff purchase 0.10½ decimals of land from the husband and daughters son of Kutiron Nessa on 30.05.1983. Plaintiff purchased 0.8½ decimals of land from khatian No. 30 in the benami of plaintiff Nos. 2 to 6. Salemat and Ali Mollah purchased 0.1½ decimals of land from khatian No. 1104 on 12.09.1983. Plaintiff purchased the same land in benami on plaintiff Nos. 2 to 6 on 30.04.1984. Plaintiff got 6 decimals of land out of 1.43 acres if land from khatian No. 1104 as heir and got 47 decimals of land from Khatian No. 30 and 36 decimals of land from Khatian No.1104 from Rupjan through Amal Nama on 15th Katrick, 1362 B.S. plaintiffs are in joint possession with co-sharers and S.A. record was not prepared correctly but it was prepared in the same of the defendants. The cause of action of the suit arose on the first part of Baishakh, 1384 B.S. when defendants denied the partition, hence suit. 

 4. Defendant Nos. 5(Ka) to (Kha) contested the suit by filing a written statement stating that Khatian No. 354 bearing plot Nos. 455/537/446 and 603 measuring an area of 1.14 acres of land originally belonged to Fazal Mollah and Karim Mollah in equal share. Karim Mollah died leaving behind Malek Mollah and others. Money Suit No. 163 of 11933 was filed against them and share of Karim Mollah was sold in money Execution Case No. 286 of 1993 and it was purchased by defendant No.5 in the benami of Chum Bala Basu and these defendants are the heirs of defendant No.5. These defendants are in possession of 0.29 decimals of land from plot No. 456, 0.42 decimals of land from plot No. 546, 0.23 decimals of land from plot No. 603, 0.12 decimals of land from plot No. 537, 0.6½ decimals of land from plot No. 455 and 0.6 decimals of land from plot No. 546, Afazuddin Mullah and Karim Mullah transferred 0.25 decimals of land to Nizamuddin by kabala dated 24.02.1947. Plaintiff gave up claim in respect of 0.12½ decimals of land of Karim Mollah in favour of those defendants. S.A record in respect of suit land was prepared correctly. These defendants have been in possession of 0.11 decimals of land out of a22 decimals of land from plot No. 545; Karim Mollah, Fazal Mollah and Nehal Uddin were the owner the owners of plot No. 554 and 555. Nehal uddin used to possess 16 annas share of plot No. 551 and 553 as homestead. Nehal Uddin Mollah also used to possess 0.46 decimals of land from plot No. 554. Karim Mollah and those defendants used to possess 0.57 decimals of land from plot No. 554 Afazuddin got 0.32 decimals of land from plot No. 1712 by amicable exchange with plot No. 844 and 854 with these defendants and transferred those lands to one Liakat Ali. The title deeds of the plaintiffs are false, collusive and the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 6. It appears from the record that plaintiff No.1 examined himself as only witness and in support of his case he filed the amolnama, kabala and Khatian. On the side of the defendants they examined 3 witnesses and produced bainanama, two kabala deeds, one DCR, a number of Khatians and a number of rent receipts in support of their case. It is the plaint case that they got the suit land by purchase through amolnama by gift and inheritance. These are modes of acquisition property by a person and it is found that the plaintiffs left no stone unturned in acquiring the suit property. It is the case of plaintiffs that they possess the suit land but the recent record of rights has been wrongly prepared. It is settled principle of law plaintiff is to prove his own case and it is also not denied that number of witnesses is not required to deny the factum one case, From the deposition of P.W.1 it is found that the plaintiffs acquired title by purchase through amolnama, by gift and by inheritance.
